official.deadline_note: Tertiary applications have now closed. The only dated window published on the official pages is the Samoa Foundation round: applications open midnight 4 August 2026 and close midday 4 September 2026 (also now closed). Education New Zealand warns that the application system may close early to countries with a large volume of applications.
official.application_cycle: Annual round with country- and region-specific dates; the 2026 tertiary round is closed and the next round's dates are not yet published
official.status_note: The official tertiary page states: 'Tertiary applications for the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship Programme have now closed.' Only the Samoa Foundation window carried dates, and that closed midday 4 September 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The awarding body states: 'With a full Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship, scholars studying in New Zealand receive: Full tuition fees.'
benefits: Living allowance to help with basic living expenses, adjusted if study commences in the home country
An establishment allowance to help with set-up costs in New Zealand, for example accommodation, textbooks or other study materials
Medical insurance while in New Zealand
Tutoring costs for additional academic support if needed

Travel to and from the home country at the start and end of the scholarship, plus travel insurance, and travel home during the scholarship for scholars studying over 1.6 years (usually one or two trips)
eligibility: Citizenship of an eligible Pacific or Asian country or region as published on the official eligible-countries page
18 years old at the time of signing the scholarship letter of offer (Samoa Foundation applicants may be 17 at commencement); there is no upper age limit, although applicants under 40 are preferred

Two years' residence in the home country prior to applying, with exceptions for those on diplomatic assignment for their home country (including dependants) and those enrolled in a course of study overseas
Postgraduate applicants must have one year of full-time or two years of part-time relevant work experience, paid, unpaid or voluntary
A commitment to contribute to the home country's social or economic development for at least two years after completing the scholarship, which is a condition of the scholarship
Not within a stand-down period from a previous Manaaki scholarship
requirements: Meet all of the published eligibility criteria before starting the application
Upload the academic transcript for the qualification applied for, including the Grading Scale (explicitly not required for Samoa Foundation applicants)
Complete the psychometric abstract reasoning and personality test within 10 days of receiving the emailed link
Attend an online video interview of roughly 40 minutes with six questions if invited
Provide an English language test score if shortlisted for tertiary study in New Zealand
documents: Academic transcript for the qualification applied for, including the Grading Scale, uploaded with the application
Verified English-translated copies of academic transcripts and completion certificates if shortlisted
English language test score from IELTS, TOEFL, PTE Academic or Cambridge Academic English (advanced) if shortlisted
Digital colour copy of passport for IELTS test applicants
selection_criteria: Strong academic ability and high grades, with qualifications that give entry to the preferred courses
Commitment to the social and economic development of the applicant's country, demonstrated clearly in the application
Choice of course aligned to the subjects recommended for the applicant's country or region
Relevant work experience in the field of study, and a qualification that progresses on from the applicant's highest existing qualification
Age 39 or younger when the scholarship starts
Integrity, resilience, communication and relationship-management skills, and the willingness and ability to adapt to a new country
coverage: Air travel to and from the home country, plus travel home during the scholarship for longer programmes
Tutoring costs and help with research and thesis costs for many postgraduate students
Reintegration allowance to help with set-up costs on return home
application_method: Complete the online eligibility questionnaire on the Manaaki site
Check the eligible countries list, then the country-specific recommended subjects
Research available courses and select study preferences in the portal
Submit the online application through the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship applicant portal
official.application_route: Online application through the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship applicant portal, following the published sequence: check eligible countries, check eligibility criteria, study subjects, research available courses, apply.
official.citizenship_residency: Open only to citizens of the eligible Pacific and Asian countries published on the official eligible-countries page, and applicants must have resided in their home country for the two years before applying, with narrow exceptions.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme exists specifically for citizens of eligible developing Pacific and Asian countries; citizens of countries not on the eligible list cannot apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only the subjects recommended for the applicant's country or region are eligible; the awarding body publishes country- and region-specific subject lists and directs applicants to check them before choosing courses.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal is required on the application form for Master's by Thesis and PhD applicants; the awarding body lists a weak research proposal as a common reason for decline. PhD applicants must also have secured, or be in active discussions with, a supervisor before the interview.
official.duration: The duration of the eligible tertiary programme of study: undergraduate degree 3-4 years, postgraduate certificate 6 months, postgraduate diploma 1 year, master's degree 1-2 years, PhD 3.5 years.
official.description: The New Zealand Government's Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships are full tertiary scholarships that enable citizens of eligible developing countries to study fulltime at a New Zealand or Pacific education institution, covering tuition fees, living and establishment allowances, insurance and travel. Scholars are expected to return home and contribute to their country's social or economic development for at least two years.
official.program_type: Government scholarship programme (tertiary strand), administered by Education New Zealand | Manapou ki te Ao
official.english_requirement: Each education institution sets its own minimum level, and the awarding body publishes only general guides: for postgraduate study, overall IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0, TOEFL iBT 90 with writing 21, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or Cambridge Academic English (advanced) overall 176 with no bands below 169; for undergraduate study, IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 80 with writing 21, PTE Academic 50 with no communicative skill below 42, or Cambridge 169 with no bands below 162. Test scores are not required at application: only shortlisted tertiary applicants must supply one, and the awarding body organises and pays for the IELTS test for shortlisted applicants from Cambodia, Indonesia, Fiji, French Pacific, Kiribati, Lao PDR, Naoero, North Pacific, Papua New Guinea, Samoa (excluding Samoa Foundation applicants), Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu.

verification.notes: All eight pages of the awarding body's own Manaaki site were read, including the tertiary student pages, eligible countries, eligibility criteria, how to apply, selection process and scholar pre-departure pages. The allowance amounts are set out in the downloadable policy handbook linked from those pages rather than on the pages themselves, so no monetary figure is recorded.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a country-restricted award, so the first filter is citizenship: the eligible Pacific and Asian country list is fixed, and the two-year home-country residence rule removes anyone currently studying or working abroad. The single most valuable thing an applicant can control is alignment: Education New Zealand publishes recommended subjects per country and states plainly that choosing courses outside them is a common reason for decline. Selection is slow and staged, running six to ten months from application close through psychometric testing and a video interview, so treat this as a full-year commitment rather than a quick application.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Working professionals from an eligible Pacific or Asian country whose job, proposed course and home-country development goals line up, and who can commit to two years' service back home.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the eligible countries list before investing any effort, and identify which of the two Pacific options applies to you
Read your country's recommended subjects page and choose courses that sit squarely inside it
Count your work experience against the postgraduate rule (one year full-time or two years part-time, paid, unpaid or voluntary) before applying
Verify the two-year residence requirement against your own history, noting the diplomatic and overseas-study exceptions
Assemble the transcript for the qualification you are applying for and check it carries a grading scale; without the scale the upload is incomplete
Book an English test early if you are shortlisted: testing can take several weeks and only shortlisted applicants are told when to sit one
common_rejection_risks: Choosing preferred courses that do not match the recommended subjects for your country or region
Not demonstrating a clear link between the proposed study and your country's social or economic development
Applying for a qualification that does not progress on from your highest existing qualification
A weak research proposal on the application form, which only affects Master's by Thesis and PhD applicants but is a named decline reason
Falling inside a stand-down period from a previous Manaaki scholarship
A low score on the psychometric abstract reasoning test, which the awarding body lists among the most common decline reasons
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Costs the awarding body explicitly does not reimburse: travel to the location of the medical check or visa interview, the police clearance fee, courier fees for the visa application, passport application or renewal fees, and any fees for dependants' visas. The institution reimburses the visa application fee, immigration levy and up to one immigration medical check fee on production of receipts.
document_audit: The transcript must include the grading scale; the awarding body calls this out as an explicit upload requirement and exempts Samoa Foundation applicants from it

English translations are only demanded at the shortlisting stage, but they must be verified translations of both transcripts and completion certificates, so start the process early rather than waiting for the request
Only shortlisted tertiary applicants need English test scores, so an applicant who books a test unnecessarily wastes money, and one who does not book after being shortlisted loses weeks
IELTS applicants must upload a digital colour copy of a valid passport, so an expiring passport can block the test booking itself
alerts: The 2026 tertiary round has closed and the next round's dates are unpublished, so any dated deadline circulating elsewhere should be treated as unverified
The awarding body warns the application system may close early for countries with a large volume of applications, so the last day is not a safe day
Accepting the offer triggers an immediate student visa application that takes two to three months and involves medical tests; a failure to obtain the visa means the scholarship is withdrawn
The two-year home-country contribution is a condition of the scholarship, not a suggestion, and the awarding body describes it as a debt-recovery obligation if not met
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Portal application with study preferences, then a multi-stage screening, psychometric test, detailed assessment, English testing and video interview, with preferred candidates finally applying for their chosen courses and a student visa.
